events.title: Fifteenth Amendment Ratified
events.description: The 15th Amendment to the U.S. Constitution was ratified. It barred federal and state governments from denying a citizen the vote because of race, color, or previous condition of servitude.
events.significance: It was a landmark of the Reconstruction era. Its promise was undercut for decades by discriminatory practices, and it became a foundation for later voting rights struggles.

events.title: U.S. Severs Diplomatic Ties with Germany
events.description: One day after Germany announced unrestricted submarine warfare, the United States broke off diplomatic relations with Berlin.
events.significance: The break was a decisive step toward American entry into World War I two months later, which helped change the course of the war.

events.title: Sinking of the USAT Dorchester
events.description: A German U-boat torpedoed the troop transport USAT Dorchester in the North Atlantic. Of the 902 men aboard, 672 died.
events.significance: It was one of the worst American losses at sea in World War II. It is remembered for the courage of its passengers and crew.

events.title: The Day the Music Died
events.description: Rock and roll stars Buddy Holly, Ritchie Valens and J. P. "The Big Bopper" Richardson died in a plane crash in Iowa.
events.significance: The deaths cut short three rising careers and marked a turning point in early rock and roll. Don McLean's song "American Pie" later made the day famous.
